outcomes.text: Within the broad topics there are suggested areas to explore; teachers do not need to cover all of them, but select areas that develop skills and use knowledge gained from other subjects.

In Paper 1, use knowledge and understanding of the topics and suggested areas to support arguments and show understanding of a wide range of issues; Paper 2 provides all the material needed to answer.

topics.title: 1 Economic, historical, moral, political and social

outcomes.text: Suggested area to explore: The role and value of history in modern society.
Suggested area to explore: Wars, conflicts and terrorism.
Suggested area to explore: The state and its institutions.
Suggested area to explore: Political systems, leadership, nationalism and forms of government.
Suggested area to explore: The role of international organisations.
Suggested area to explore: The provision and politics of aid.
Suggested area to explore: Justice and the justice system; prison and rehabilitation.
Suggested area to explore: The role of the individual in society.
Suggested area to explore: Family, marriage and partnerships, social pressure, class and social attitudes.
Suggested area to explore: Globalisation and its impacts.
Suggested area to explore: Wealth and equality in society.
Suggested area to explore: Population and migration.
Suggested area to explore: Education.
Suggested area to explore: Welfare.
Suggested area to explore: Sport and leisure.
Suggested area to explore: Work and employment.
Suggested area to explore: Industry and commerce.
Suggested area to explore: Freedom of speech, thought and action.
Suggested area to explore: Human rights.
Suggested area to explore: Animal welfare.
Suggested area to explore: Matters of conscience, faith and tolerance.

topics.title: 2 Science, including its history, philosophy, ethics, general principles and applications; environmental issues; technology and mathematics

outcomes.text: Suggested area to explore: Medical and scientific advances and their ethics.
Suggested area to explore: Drug testing, manufacture and provision.
Suggested area to explore: Diet, health education and provision of healthcare.
Suggested area to explore: Space exploration and its associated industry.
Suggested area to explore: Information and communications technology.
Suggested area to explore: Surveillance and privacy.
Suggested area to explore: Environmental concerns.
Suggested area to explore: Natural disasters including mitigation and management.
Suggested area to explore: Rural and urban concerns.
Suggested area to explore: Food and water security.
Suggested area to explore: Transport, travel and tourism.
Suggested area to explore: The uses and applications of mathematics.

topics.title: 3 Literature, language, the arts, crafts, and the media

outcomes.text: Suggested area to explore: Literature.
Suggested area to explore: Non-fiction writing.
Suggested area to explore: Language.
Suggested area to explore: Performing arts.
Suggested area to explore: Visual arts.
Suggested area to explore: Applied arts.
Suggested area to explore: Arts institutions and venues.
Suggested area to explore: Traditional arts and crafts; heritage.
Suggested area to explore: Print and digital media.
Suggested area to explore: Advertising.
Suggested area to explore: Censorship and freedom of the media and the arts.
Develop the ability to identify, select and apply appropriate information to respond to a task.
Understand different points of view on a topic.
Use information as evidence to support an argument with examples and to develop ideas.
Read widely for general understanding and develop skills to identify relevant information from a variety of sources.
Develop a wide range of vocabulary in English and the ability to understand the use of English words and phrases in context.
Understand how information is presented and how the English language is used to convey implicit as well as explicit meaning.
Develop the ability to analyse data, interpret information and offer key points.
Learn skills of evaluation, going beyond observing or summarising the evidence.
Learn to draw out inferences, understand the implications of a course of action, develop and draw out the significance of an argument and examine other points of view.
Learn to make supported judgements.
Develop the skills to write in accurate English in a clear, coherent and structured way, including essays.
Learn to write shorter responses for a variety of purposes, which might include explanation, description, summary, analysis, evaluation and persuasion.
Learn to use a range of vocabulary, appropriate spelling, grammar and punctuation, and use of register, to communicate information, ideas and opinions appropriate to the task.
